To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the three-dimensional structure of a ternary complex consisting human alpha-thrombins, hirugen, and the active-site thrombin inhibitor RWJ- 51438 was determined at 1,7 A resolution.
the three-dimensional structure of human alpha-thombin, hirugen, and the active-site inhibiter RWJ-514388 has been determined at a 1.7A resolution.
the ketone carbony group of the inhibitor RWJ- 51438 forms a hemiketal structure with Ser195 and that the inhibitor's carboxylate forms a salt bridge with the Lys60F residue.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of thrombin in complex with RWJ- 51438, a potent and selective thrombin inhibitor that is currently undergoing clinical trials.
the structure of thrombin, the structure of the thrombin-inhibitor complex, and the effects of the insertion loop on the structure of thrombomodulin.
the structure and dynamics of proteins and nucleic acids and the interactions between these molecules and their ligands.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the structure of the complex of RWJ-41438 and thrombin is consistent with the mechanism of action for thrombin inhibitors of this class and that the structure of this complex is a model for the design of more effective and potent thrombin inhibitors.
RWJ-51439 is a very effective and potent anticoagulant agent, which has the potential to be used in a clinical setting.

the inhibitor RWJ- 51438, in the ternary complex with thrombin, induces a perturbation in the 60A insertion loop that is different from the perturbation induced in the 60B insertion loop by the inhibitor RWJ 56604, as previously described in the ternary complexes of thrombin with RWJ-56604 and hirugen or hirudin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have determined the structure of a ternary thrombin complex with a new active-site inhibitor RW51438, and we have found a unique perturbation on the 60A to 60I insertion loop of thrombin, caused by the carboxyl group of RW51438.

we have solved the three-dimensional structures for the ternary complex of human alpha-thombin, hirugen, and RWJ-5143, which has a tetrahedral hemiketal covalent intermediate structure and a salt bridge between Lys60F and the carboxyl group of RWJ-51,438.
the structure of the thrombin-hirugen-RWJ-51438 ternary complex is the first reported structure of a thrombin-hirudin complex with an active-site inhibitor covalently bound to the enzyme.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the insertion loop of thrombin is flexible enough to accommodate a bulky carboxylate group of RWJ-61438.
a single point mutation of Lys60F to Ala60F can significantly alter the conformation of the 60-loop, thereby affecting the binding of RWJ-41438 to human alpha-thrombins.
the 60A insertion loop is highly flexible and can be perturbed by small molecules.
